## Pass 1

Changes (unit · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done). Units are numbered from 0 as in units.json. All edits made by script (/tmp/claude-0/reviewer1/edit*.py), which asserts each old string before replacing it.

- U0 · p · style · p:true on a unit that continues the speech begun in ani-001-a, U3 (conventions: p only on the first unit of a chapter, rubric or speech; 001-a's later "I am …" units have none) · p removed.
- U4 · l / i / n · minor · "ḏḥwty smꜣꜥ-ḫrw wsir … with the subject first: 'Thoth makes Osiris true of voice'" treats a noun followed by a verb with no suffix as a finite clause. That form is a participle: a participial statement · l "Thoth · who-makes-true-of-voice"; i "it is Thoth who makes Osiris true of voice …"; the note now gives the form and points to "I am Thoth, who makes Osiris true of voice" in the first half. wḏ is now labelled sḏm·f.
- U28 · l / i / n · minor · "The negated passive can be a statement or a wish; … a wish is taken": a wish is not denied with n. n + sḏm·f mostly denies the past, and among the wishes it reads as future (as nn would) · l "not · shall-be-repelled-he · …"; i "He shall not be repelled, he shall not be turned back."; the note sentence replaced.
- U19, U22, U24 · l / i / n · minor · "perfected" for mnḫw is Budge's English ("menχu, perfected") · → "effective" (l "the-bas · effective", i "the effective bas"); U19 note "mnḫw 'effective, excellent' (Budge: 'perfected')". "excellent" stays with iqr in U20.
- U8, U14 · words[rꜣ-sṯꜣw] glyph D21 · minor · coded phon "r", but the reading is rꜣ and the published introduction and address code the mouth in this name log "rꜣ", as U8's own rꜣ 'door' does · role → log, tr → "rꜣ"; U8 note "the mouth rꜣ with a stroke".
- U23 · words[trwy] glyphs X1, D21, M6 · minor · roles inverted: the uniliterals t and r were phon and the plant tr (M6) was comp "repeating t and r". Conventions make the complement the uniliteral, and the hymn to Ra codes the same word X1 comp, D21 comp, M6 phon · X1, D21 → comp; M6 → phon; note now "the plant tr (M6) with t and r before it as complements".
- U10 · n · minor · "sḫm, here with the owl m, as in line 21": line 21 has the sign Aa15 for m, not the owl · now "sḫm as in line 21, here with the owl m in place of Aa15, …".
- U29 · n · minor · "pr·f has w before the legs, as in line 22": in line 22 the w comes after the legs · now "pr·f has a chick w that is not read, as pr·i in line 22 (there after the legs)".
- U1 · n · minor · iwr·i 'I was conceived' was given no form label, though only a passive gives that sense · added "a passive sḏm·f like msy·i".
- U17 · n · minor · ḫrp is translated as a plural ("of the Directors") with no word on the missing plural · added "(the sceptre S42; plural not written)". The note was also trimmed from 1278 to 1096 characters (the swallow, the mouth and t of rdit, Budge's numeral, the separate "ḥr 'upon'" were removed); no reading changed.
- U2 · n · style · 1256 characters (over the WARN limit) · trimmed to 1090. The tense remark is kept, but the routine ḥnꜥ gloss is dropped. Added that Budge's footnote variants have different signs where iḏbwy stands (footnote 1, p. 21, in the established file), which is a further reason for doubt.
- U9 · l · style · m 'in' had no item in l ("Horus · protecting") · "Horus · in · protecting".
- U13 · n · style · removed the establishment remark "Budge's italic does not show clearly whether he printed q or g, but the sign is q": the sign is q, and the remark tells the reader nothing about the word.
- U33 · words[sšw·ṯi] glyphs V13, M17 · style · the stative ending was coded phon "ṯ" / "i"; the published address codes the same ending (smi·ṯi) suff "·ṯ" / "i" · roles → suff, tr "·ṯ", "i".
- U21 · words[mꜣꜣ·f] say · style · "maaf"; published mꜣꜣ·f (introduction) is "maaef" · → maaef.
- U28 · say · style · "khesefetuf", "shenatuf": published ·tw·f forms say -tuef (denituef, setatuef) · → khesefetuef, shenatuef.
- U29 · say · style · "maa-kheruf"; published ·f after w is -uef (kheftyuef, iuef) · → maa-kheruef.

Rulings on the drafter's points:
- p:true on line 13: removed (above). The unit continues a speech, and the build needs no p on a part's first unit.
- Z15e in snwt: kept log, tr "snw". The six strokes do not count anything here. With n, t and the festival classifier they write the name of the sixth-day feast, so they are a word-sign. num is for numerals, and that is not how the strokes are used. Budge's three groups (VI / ent / ḥeb) are rightly joined: a genitive after masculine hrw would be n, not nt, so the n-t belongs to snwt. q re-indexed correctly (0-1:2-3:4).
- ḥmwt for Budge's āb (U17): kept, doubtful. The printed sign is not U23's ꜣb chisel (the establisher says ankh/stand-like with a knob on top). The drill ḥm with a seated man gives the title of the high priest of Ptah, and the Sokar feast and Memphis around it fit. The note marks the sign as doubtful. U23 log tr "ḥmt" follows the 001-a precedent (O26 phon ꜥḥꜥ): a sign keeps the code the print shows, the tr gives what it stands for, and the note says so.
- imyw for Budge's ammu "flames" (U10): kept. M17 Z11 G17 G43 + god classifier spell i-im-m-w, the plural nisba. The address codes imyw the same way (M17 comp, Z11 phon, G17 comp). No sign gives Budge's "flames".
- ḥsw / mrw statives (U29): kept. W14 ḥs with ḥ and s complements plus w, and the hoe mr with r plus w, each followed by the man with hand to mouth, are 3rd masculine singular statives describing the subject of ꜥq·f / pr·f. Budge's "as he pleaseth / desireth" would need a suffix or a relative form, and there is none.
- wpyw for àpui (U24): kept. Budge's àp is his old value of the horns F13. The complements p and w after it confirm wp.
- mṯnw for mātennu (U24, U26): kept as doubtful. t-n-nw-w with the road sign gives the road word; the m+arm ligature is coded as printed and the arm is not read; the note says t stands for ṯ.
- gm·n·tw (U32): kept. G28 gm, m complement, n, t, w = sḏm·n·tw·f, correctly labelled and given both senses. The past rendering is acceptable for this text, and the note gives "cannot be found".
- iwr·i joining āu + àm-à (U1): kept as a slip (one sense, fixed by the parallel msy·i m ḏdw). The note opens with the formula and says how the surplus i-m arose is not sure.
- rḫtt (U2): kept as doubtful. The text writes only cords + t + town; footnote variant 2 (r, ḫ, t, t, cord) supports it.
- iḏbwy (U2): kept as doubtful, with the footnote added (above).
- sšw·ṯi (U33): kept. G37 is the classifier of šw 'empty', the s-causative gives sšw 'make empty', and V13 + reed is the 3rd feminine stative ending agreeing with mḫꜣt. The second s standing for š is opened with the formula and called doubtful.

Considered and refused:
- U0/U1 R11 doubled coded comp "ḏd": the introduction codes ḏdt the same way (the hymn to Osiris has det). Accepted; the note's "not read again" describes what a complement is.
- U17 rdit with D36 tr "di": a sign used for the giving arm. The 001-a ink precedent (W24 tr "in") gives the meant value, and the note opens with the slip formula. Kept.
- U30 wḏt·f, first hand coded comp "d" after wḏ (which has ḏ): d for ḏ is a common late spelling, and the note calls it the complement. Kept.
- U26 ḥtp-nṯr with R8 and R4 log, where the hymn to Ra and the address have phon: each sign here writes its whole word with no complement, which is log by conventions. Kept.
- Surplus signs keeping phon tr (U1 i, m; U7 second swallow; U9 nw in nḏ; U13 reeds in sqꜣ; U18 reeds; U29 w in pr·f; U31 t in ḏd·f): house practice allows phon with a "not read" note (001-a pass 1). Kept.
- U9 S34 phon "ꜣb" in iꜣby: printed like the ankh where the U23 chisel is expected. The hymn to Osiris codes ꜣbḏw with S34 phon ꜣb in the same way. Kept.
- U12 ꜥbt 'offerings(?)', U13 rrw gap, U27 dnd gap, U8 sšyt '(?)', U17 mꜥḫꜣyt·f: the doubts are marked and the gaps are honest. Kept. U27's "a word dnd 'rage' has this spelling" was not verified against a lexicon (none may be opened); it is left for pass 2 to judge.
- U5 wḏ·tw + ir n·i ḏḥwty: the grammar is sound (dative pronoun before the noun subject), and the alternative ir·n·i is noted. Kept.
- U11 nw (plural genitive) agreeing with unwritten plural ḥbw: sound. Kept.
- U16 m iry·f 'as his attendant(?)': iry is the nisba of r, as in known lemmas; the doubt is marked. Kept.
- U18 nni-nsw, say Neni-nesu: identical to the published Spell 125 declarations. The X1 is the t of nswt, which the published reading also leaves out. Kept.
- U32 im 'there', U33 iw left out of l: house practice (the address and the introduction leave iw out of l). Kept.
- Names and say forms checked against the published parts: Busiris/Djedu, Rosetau/Ra-setjau, Heliopolis/Iunu, Abydos/Abedju (R17 log as in the hymn to Osiris), Sokar, Herakleopolis, tpḥt (Spell 125 declarations, tpḥt-f), trwy teruy, nṯrw (single flag + god coded log, as 001-a U8). All match.
- No Budge-isms left in l / i ("triumphant", "saith", "homage", "victorious", "thee/ye", "hath": none). Budge's English appears only in the notes, quoted as his.

Re-check: the concatenated glyph codes of units.json equal the established sequence exactly (932 signs). The q of every word that keeps Budge's division equals the established q, and the 8 joined or split words are correctly re-indexed (iwr·i, iḏbwy/rḫtt, wḏ·tw, ir/n·i, snwt, ḥtp-nṯr). Restored flags: R8 (l. 39), E34 N35 G37 of wn·f (l. 43), I9 of sp·f (l. 44). 25 rubric words, as established. Morph indices cover every glyph. No note is over 1100 characters (largest: U17 1096, U2 1090, U9 1023).
